# commons-json — LLM/AI quick reference

Greenfossil's Scala 3 JSON AST and codec. Import:

```scala
import com.greenfossil.commons.json.*
import scala.util.{Failure, Success, Try}
```

## Types

`JsValue` → `JsObject` | `JsArray` | `JsString` | `JsNumber` | `JsBoolean` | `JsNull` | `JsTemporal` | `JsUndefined`.

`JsObject` preserves field order (`ListMap`); `JsUndefined` is the missing-path sentinel.

## Construction

```scala
Json.obj("name" -> "Ada", "age" -> 42, "tags" -> Json.arr("scala", "json"))
Json.arr(1, 2, 3)
Json.parse("""{"ok":true}""")
```

`Json.obj` drops `None`; `null` becomes JSON `null`. `Json.arr` drops `None` and empty optional arrays.

## Reading

```scala
val value = Json.parse(input).as[JsObject]
value("user")("name").asTextOpt            // chained field access
value.at("/user/name").asTextOpt          // RFC 6901 JSON Pointer
value \ "user" \ "name"                    // `\` path access
value.as[MyCaseClass]                     // codec extraction
value("missing").toOption                 // None (JsUndefined)
```

Typed accessors: `asTextOpt`, `asIntOpt`, `asBooleanOpt`, `asSeqOpt[T]`, `asJsObjectOpt`, `asJsArrayOpt`; defaulting variants end in `OrEmpty` / `OrElse`.

## Structured lookup and errors

```scala
val pointer = JsonPointer.parse("/payload/question").get
pointer.select(value) match
  case Success(v)    => v.asText
  case Failure(err)  => err.asInstanceOf[JsonAccessError].path

JsonPointer.parse("/a~1b")   // Try[JsonPointer]; escapes ~ and / per RFC 6901
JsonPointer.escape("a/b")    // "a~1b"
```

`JsonPointer.select` returns `Try[JsValue]`: a missing path is
`Failure(JsonAccessError)`, while a real `null` is `Success(JsNull)`. Use
`selectOpt` when absence is expected.

## AI/streaming helpers

```scala
Json.canonical(value)        // recursively sorted object keys, arrays keep order
Json.canonicalString(value)  // deterministic compact JSON

Json.parseTry(text)          // Try[JsValue] — String
Json.parseTry(bytes)         // Try[JsValue] — Array[Byte]
Json.parseTry(stream)        // Try[JsValue] — InputStream
Json.parseBase64URLTry(b64)  // Try[JsValue] — URL-safe Base64
Json.parseBase64URLTry(b64, charset)
Json.parseBase64URLTry(bytes, charset)
Json.parseLines(text)        // Seq[Try[JsValue]], one per non-blank line
Json.stringifyLines(values)  // one compact JSON value per line
```

Use canonical output for hashing/caching/replay; use JSONL for event/trajectory streams. A malformed line is `Failure(JsonLineError(...))` carrying its 1-based line number and original input.

## Writing

```scala
Json.stringify(value)        // compact
Json.prettyPrint(value)      // indented
Json.toBytes(value)
value.stringify
```

## Jackson 3 compatibility

commons-json 1.5.0-RC1 uses Jackson 3 (`tools.jackson`) internally. It can
coexist with the Jackson 2 used by Armeria. `json-path` uses its Jackson 3
providers. The public `JsValue`/`Json` API is unchanged; `JsValue._jsonNode`
and `jsonNodeToJsValue` are internal helpers and now use
`tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode`.

Jackson 2 parsing defaults are retained, including exact BigDecimal values and
trailing-token behavior. See `docs/jackson3-migration.md`.

## Pitfalls

- `apply`/`\` return `JsUndefined` for missing paths; use `toOption` or `JsonPointer.selectOpt` when absence matters.
- `as[T]` throws `JsonException`; prefer `asOpt[T]` for model/tool input.
- Object key order is insertion order unless you call `Json.canonical`.
- JSONL is newline-delimited **values**, not a single JSON array; blank lines are ignored.
